jobs.description:

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

 - We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

 - We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

 - We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.


THE ROLE 

Legora is seeking a Partner Program Manager to design, launch, and refine the operational backbone of our rapidly expanding partner ecosystem. Working directly within our VP of Partnerships, you’ll take high-level go-to-market strategies and convert them into actionable, turnkey frameworks for our tech, consulting, education, and cloud & AI alliances.

Your mission is to make partner collaboration frictionless, predictable, and directly tied to customer success. By bridging internal strategy with external execution, you’ll serve as the primary glue connecting Partnerships with Revenue, Product, Marketing, and Success teams. If you’re excited to build the playbook, metrics, and enablements that will define how an AI market-leader collaborates at scale, this role is for you.




WHAT YOU’LL DO 

 - Build & Scale the Program: Stand up and own our core partner program framework from scratch, creating clear tiering, governance, benefits, and operational rules of engagement.

 - Connect Strategic Dots: Drive day-to-day program execution while establishing the architecture, incentives, and processes needed to transition from a lean early-stage program to an enterprise-grade ecosystem.

 - End-to-End Program Ownership: Manage the full partner lifecycle—from onboarding workflows and portal operations to performance tracking, deal registration, and co-sell workflows.

 - Scale into Leadership: Operate as a high-impact individual contributor with a potential pathway to step into a formal partner leadership role as the organization expands over the next 6–12 months.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5+ years of experience in Partner Program Management, Channel Operations, or Partner Ecosystem Development.

 - Proven program builder experience at a growth-stage or mid-market company (building frameworks, incentives, and workflows without relying on mega-tech resources). Has been part of building a partner program from the foundation to a scaled system.

 - Execution + Strategy Mix: Strong operational foundation with the ability to build processes, manage PRMs/tools, and solve tactical friction while keeping long-term growth goals in mind.

 - Leadership Potential: Demonstrated track record of cross-functional influence, business acumen, and readiness to grow into a team lead or managerial role as the team scales.




WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU

 - Global collaboration: Partner with teams and clients across Europe, APAC, and North America.

 - Competitive package: Comprehensive salary, benefits, and tools for success.

 - Meaningful work: Your efforts shape how thousands of lawyers use AI daily.

 - In-person environment: Union Square office designed for ambitious builders and company provided lunch daily.

 - Benefits & Perks: We invest in our people with a comprehensive, thoughtfully designed benefits package:
   Medical, Dental & Vision
   
   - Multiple medical plan options through Aetna and Kaiser Permanente
   
   - HSA or Healthcare FSA (based on plan selection)
   
   - Dental plans via MetLife
   
   - Vision plans via Vision Care
   
   Family Support
   
   - Generous parental leave
   
   - Free access to Maven Clinic
   
   - Dependent Care FSA
   
   - Free One Medical membership for employees and dependents

   - Pre-tax commuter benefits
   
   - Life Insurance + STD/LTD

Joining Legora means three things.

 - We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

The role
This role owns how it works to be an employee at Legora on the backend. You will operationalise every stage of the employee journey,  making sure every moment is supported by clean systems, accurate data, and processes that scale. If an employee interacts with a Legora program or system, from their first day in the HRIS to a salary change three years in, your team is accountable for making it accurate, timely, and smooth.

You will lead a distributed People Operations team across Stockholm and New York, reporting to the VP, People Operations. As we enter new markets, you will also build and manage local specialisms to handle day-to-day employee and manager questions and run structured, lower-complexity casework, with a clean handoff to Employee Relations for anything that becomes formal, contested, or carries legal weight.



What you'll own

 - The full employee lifecycle, operationally. Every touchpoint from offer to exit, mapped, documented, and supported end to end.

 - HRIS and data integrity. Onboarding new hires into the HRIS, data entry, and data QA. You keep employee data accurate, complete, and audit-ready as the single source of truth.

 - Contracts and changes. Addendums, employee transfers, salary and reporting-line changes, and the workflows and documentation behind each one, working in close partnership with Payroll so every change flows through accurately and on time.

 - Benefits and leave administration. Run the day-to-day administration of benefits and leave across our markets. Total Rewards owns the policies, plan design, and philosophy; your team makes sure they are executed cleanly for every employee. Anything contested, discriminatory, or medically complex is escalated to Employee Relations.

 - Local HR Generalist build-out. As Legora enters new markets, hire, ramp, and manage the local HR Generalist / People Advisor-Ops layer: the in-market presence for day-to-day employee and manager questions, and for structured, lower-complexity casework such as absence management, recurring capability concerns, and restructuring conversations. These roles report into People Operations for management and delivery, with a dotted line to the regional Employee Relations Director for sign-off on jurisdictional readiness and casework quality.

 - Systems and tooling. Run the People tech stack (HiBob, Ashby, Ironclad), drive adoption, and take manual work out of the process.

 - Process and SOPs. Design scalable, well-documented processes for every program employees touch, and keep reducing friction and cycle time.

 - Compliance and controls. Partner with Legal and Finance to keep operations compliant across our markets, including working time, leave, and entity or EOR transitions, with a clean escalation path to Employee Relations for anything that becomes formal or carries legal weight.

 - Reporting. Own people data quality and the reporting backbone that powers People analytics for the business.
   


What you'll bring

 - 8+ years in People Operations or HR Operations, including leading a team and building out local, in-market HR capability as a company scales into new geographies, ideally in a high-growth or global company.

 - Deep HRIS expertise across complex, multidisciplinary system landscapes, with a strong interest in data quality, integrations, AI and tools.

 - A track record of building and scaling lifecycle processes and SOPs internationally, and of moving work from manual to automated.

 - Strong grasp of multi-jurisdiction employment compliance across EMEA, AMER, and APAC.

 - Comfort operating in a tiered People model, with clear judgment on what your team owns directly and what belongs with Employee Relations, Legal, or Total Rewards.

 - An operator's mindset: detail-obsessed, systems-thinking, and a high bar for accuracy.

 - Comfort partnering across Finance, Legal, and IT, and communicating clearly with employees and leaders alike.

 - Fluency in English, which is our working language.
   

Why this role
 People Operations is the infrastructure that lets the rest of the People team, and the business, move fast without breaking things. That now includes building the in-market HR Generalist presence that gives every employee fast, consistent support close to home, wherever they are, with a clean handoff to Employee Relations the moment something becomes formal. You will build that infrastructure for one of the most exciting companies in tech, and set the standard for what operational excellence looks like as we scale.

We’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer and committed to creating an inclusive, high-performance culture where everyone can do their best work. If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.


ABOUT THE ROLE

The Statutory Reporting & Compliance Manager sits within the accounting function and owns statutory reporting and regulatory compliance for the group's legal entities. You will be responsible for the local accounts of assigned entities and the full calendar of statutory and regulatory deliverables. As we enter new markets, you will assess and stand up the local reporting, registration, and compliance requirements from scratch.

You set the standard for how statutory work is done at Legora — the processes, controls, and documentation — and you are the central point of contact for advisors and local authorities. It is a role for someone who likes structure, deadlines, and being the person who knows exactly what is due, where, and why.

 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

Statutory accounts & local books

 - Coordinate preparation of statutory financial statements for assigned legal entities under local legislation and requirements (e.g., UK FRS 102, Swedish K3, German HGB, French PCG)

 - Prepare and file annual reports, supplemental statements, and required exhibits with local authorities

 - Own the completeness and accuracy of local books and accounting records, including statutory adjustments, and keep account balances reconciled and substantiated

Regulatory compliance & market expansion

 - Own the group compliance calendar: statutory deliverables, statistical reporting, and other government filings across all entities

 - Monitor legislative and regulatory changes in our jurisdictions, assess their impact, and implement the accounting process and control changes they require

 - Assess statutory, registration, and reporting requirements for new markets ahead of expansion, and stand up compliant local processes

 - Coordinate with local advisors and consultants on preparation and filing of statutory documents

Controls, audit & documentation

 - Act as the primary contact for local authorities on audits, new legislation, and ad-hoc requests

 - Develop, implement, and monitor internal control policies and procedures appropriate for our stage, and ensure they are consistently followed

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 7+ years of experience in statutory accounting, audit, or financial reporting, with demonstrated ownership of entity-level statutory deliverables end to end

 - Experience managing statutory compliance across multiple countries, directly or through local advisors

 - Strong knowledge of statutory reporting in at least one of our jurisdictions

 - Track record of working directly with external advisors, and local authorities

 - Experience implementing or improving accounting processes and internal controls

 - Highly organized and deadline-driven — you run a compliance calendar, not the other way around

 - Clear written communication: you can turn a legislative change or technical question into guidance the rest of the team can follow

Nice to have

 - Experience in a multi-entity international group spanning Europe, North America, and Asia-Pacific

 - Familiarity with statutory frameworks in several of our jurisdictions (e.g., UK FRS 102, German HGB, French PCG, Italian OIC, Spanish PGC, Indian Companies Act reporting, or Australian requirements)

 - Qualification such as CPA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent

 - Experience standing up statutory compliance in a new market or jurisdiction
